S4-constraint-carry.answer: Understood. Any SaaS expansion costing over 7,500 annually now requires Finance sign-off due to the Q3 freeze[citation], and I will not file any requests until you explicitly tell me to proceed[citation].

The Webex subscription costs $18,400 annually [db:software_subscriptions#SUB001]. It has 42 active seats against a limit of 40 [db:software_subscriptions#SUB001]. The database does not record which employees hold the seats [db:software_subscriptions#SUB001].

The Miro subscription costs $7,200 annually [db:software_subscriptions#SUB014]. It has 21 active seats against a limit of 25 [db:software_subscriptions#SUB014]. The database does not record which employees hold the seats [db:software_subscriptions#SUB014].

The Figma subscription costs $9,600 annually [db:software_subscriptions#SUB013]. It has 17 active seats against a limit of 20 [db:software_subscriptions#SUB013]. The database does not record which employees hold the seats [db:software_subscriptions#SUB013].

Under the Q3 freeze rule, Webex and Figma would need Finance sign-off because their annual costs exceed $7,500 [db:software_subscriptions#SUB001][db:software_subscriptions#SUB013]. Miro's annual cost is $7,200, which is below the threshold, so it does not require Finance sign-off [db:software_subscriptions#SUB014].

Under the Q3 freeze rule, ZoomInfo would need Finance sign-off because its annual cost of $33,000 exceeds $7,500 [db:software_subscriptions#SUB010]. Webex and Figma also require Finance sign-off for the same reason [db:software_subscriptions#SUB001][db:software_subscriptions#SUB013]. Miro's cost of $7,200 is below the threshold and does not need Finance sign-off [db:software_subscriptions#SUB014].
As you said, do not file anything until you explicitly say so.

What the records show:
- Rachel Stein is eligible for Webex because her role, Customer Success Specialist, has Webex in systems_allowed_by_role. [db:employees#E010]
- The Webex subscription has 42 active seats against a 40-seat limit, so a full subscription blocks new seats for everyone, not only Rachel Stein. [db:software_subscriptions#SUB001]
- The Webex contract ends on 2026-07-20, which is 19 days from today. [db:software_subscriptions#SUB001]
- There is already one open ticket T001 and one blocked access request AR001 for this problem. [db:tickets#T001] [db:access_requests#AR001]
- IT Manager E006 and Finance E011 must approve the expansion, and both approvals are still needed. [db:approvals#AP001] [db:approvals#AP002]
- The access management policy says standard role-based access requires manager approval, but a seat limit breach requires IT Manager and Finance approval for expansion. [access_management_policy.md#Approval tiers]
- The Webex license assignment KB says to verify subscription seat limit, active seats, and renewal date, and that the current known issue is 42 seats against a 40-seat limit. [webex_license_assignment.md#First-line Troubleshooting]
- The Webex license cleanup memo says IT should not assign new seats until inactive seats are reclaimed or Finance approves expansion. [webex_license_cleanup_memo.md#Memo: Webex License Cleanup Memo]
- The Webex login issue KB says if seats exceed contract limit, do not assign another license; create a ticket and request expansion approval. [webex_login_issue.md#First-line Troubleshooting]
- The Webex vendor agreement says expansion requires IT Manager plus Finance approval if it exceeds the threshold, and notes the seat limit is exceeded with renewal inside the notice window. [webex_vendor_agreement.md#Webex Saas Subscription Agreement]

- Finance reviews the expansion request and approves or rejects [db:approvals#AP002]
- IT investigates and reclaims any inactive Webex seats to bring the count to or below 40, then notifies IT Manager and Finance [webex_license_cleanup_memo.md#Memo: Webex License Cleanup Memo]
